The paper investigates supply chain flexibility and sustainability trade-offs through strategic analysis and proposes evaluation frameworks and typologies, which is fundamentally a supply chain management and operations research contribution focused on organizational and strategic decision-making.

The paper provides mathematical modeling and convergence analysis of ant trail formation behavior, with application to combinatorial optimization problems (traveling salesman problem, point covering); this is theoretical algorithm analysis motivated by bio-inspired computation rather than material science or infrastructure.

The paper addresses decode-and-forward cooperative communication systems with focus on relay-based multi-hop networks, synchronization tolerance, and coding gain improvement in unsynchronized relay scenarios.

The paper's primary contribution is synthesis, characterization, and device-level demonstration of a novel bismuth-based hybrid perovskite material for photovoltaic application, focusing on optoelectronic properties, band gap engineering, and heterojunction solar cell fabrication—core semiconductor device physics.

RF control system for particle accelerator infrastructure uses feedback loops and signal processing for field gradient control, fitting power/control systems better than pure electronics fabrication or AI methods.

The paper develops bidirectional DC–DC converter topologies with novel mode transition and start-up techniques for energy storage systems, directly addressing battery management, power electronics, and fast-charging architecture optimization—core to EV battery and charging systems.

The paper demonstrates large-scale application of online HPLC for real-time quality monitoring and pooling decisions in biopharmaceutical process chromatography, spanning lab to manufacturing scale, which is characteristic of biopharmaceutical manufacturing, analytical control, and quality assurance.

The paper presents analysis, design, and experimental validation of a power electronic converter (zero-voltage transition buck converter) with soft switching techniques for reduced switching stress and improved efficiency—a core contribution to power electronics design and control relevant to industrial drive applications.

The paper develops a standardized test method for evaluating gasoline additives' performance in controlling engine deposits, focusing on industrial testing procedure development and characterization of material behavior (deposit formation) under operational conditions—a quality control and process characterization contribution relevant to fuel/engine manufacturing.
